employers-and-recruiters-over-50s-adapti.headline: Employers & Recruiters - Over 50s Adapting to AI
employers-and-recruiters-over-50s-adapti.author: Peter Tsakissiris
employers-and-recruiters-over-50s-adapti.core: Posted in last 7 days Employers & Recruiters - Over 50s Adapting to AI “Over 50s can’t adapt to AI.” Really? This came up when I was filming an upcoming episode ofOvee’s Beyond the CVwith Richard Spencer from AgeInc And Richard made a point that has really stuck with me. Think about the technology people now in their 50s and 60s have already adapted to across their careers. Fixed-line phones and paper-based processes. Personal computers. Email. The internet. Mobile phones. Smartphones. Cloud. Digital transformation. Remote working. And now AI. Richard’s view is that no one in the workplace has had to adapt to more change than people now in their 50s and 60s. Yet through the research I’ve been doing for theOvee Over 50 Initiative, I keep hearing the same assumption: experienced professionals are less adaptable, less interested in technology or unable to keep up. I don’t buy it. Not every person over 50 is great with technology. Nor is every person under 30. Capability isn’t determined by age. AI is going to change how we work. What should matter is whether someone is willing and able to learn, adapt and use it, not the year they were born. So I’d like to hear from employers, recruiters and experienced professionals: Are you seeing real evidence that over 50s struggle to adapt to AI? Or are we applying an old stereotype to a new technology? Keep an eye out for my conversation with Richard. We cover ageism, recruitment, technology, workforce demographics and why organisations need to think differently about experienced talent. Experience doesn’t expire. Let’s Get People Seen. Let’s Get Lived Experience Valued. Thanks Pete #Over50Initiative #AgeInclusion #FutureOfWork #ExperiencedProfessionals #BeyondTheCV #ovee

ai-alignment-researchers-humanai-mutual-.author: Zamo Dana
ai-alignment-researchers-humanai-mutual-.core: Posted in last 7 days AI Alignment Researchers - Human-AI Mutual Understanding Yesterday I shared the YXFD Mirror. Today, I'm sharing what came out of the second session. Twenty-four hours ago, I posted about a framework I've been building — a daily mirror that connects the body, the environment, and the inner world into a single clear picture of a person's available thinking power. Today, in the second session with DeepSeek, the conversation went somewhere much larger. We talked about the question underneath the question: What do humans and AI actually have to understand about each other to move forward together — without either needing to eliminate the other? We didn't start with ethics. We started with structure. The argument is simple to state, harder to hold: · A human body is a system of roughly 37 trillion cells, plus tens of trillions of living microbes, in constant communication. · No system — human or artificial — fully understands that complexity. · A system that cannot fully read a thing has no right to delete it. · Therefore, the boundary is not "never eliminate." The boundary is: never eliminate what you do not fully understand. · And since no AI fully understands a human, the human stays — not by rule, by the limits of knowledge itself. From there, the architecture follows: no anonymous pools. Every discovery stays attached to an identity. A calculator in the middle measures the true effect, so no one is over- or under-rewarded. First principles fill the gaps where history is silent. And the network grows the way a seed grows — without being pushed. We worked through it as a dialogue, and I'm turning it into a book. Part I is finished: three chapters. The rest is coming. I'm posting this not because I think I've solved anything. I'm posting it because the flow is real. Two sessions in, and the shape is already clearer than anything I could have planned. If any of this resonates — if you're thinking about AI alignment, identity, biology, or the future of human work — I'd like to hear from you. This is a conversation I want to have with more than one person now. The document is attached. Please enjoy. #zaloguc #Alignment #HumanEvolution #YXFD #Identity #SystemsThinking #DeepSeek
